segments.text: Hi.
Three weeks.
Twenty-one mornings without it.
Twenty-one evenings.
A weekend or three.
Think how many times, in three weeks, an old cue fired and you did something else.
Here's what all those moments have been doing.
In the prep week you saw how the autopilot was built.
A cue, then nicotine, then relief.
Repeated so many times that it ran by itself.
For three weeks you've been running a different version.
A cue, then a breath.
A cue, then a glass of water, or a walk, or just waiting.
Every time, the old link got a little weaker, and a new one got a little stronger.
That's what I mean by rewiring.
Nothing mysterious.
Practice.
And you've had a great deal of practice.
It isn't finished.
Some links are stubborn, and some cues haven't come round yet.
But the direction is clear, and you're the one who set it.
I'd like you to see how much you're carrying now.
As I name each one, notice which you've actually used.
Checking the basics first.
Food, water, sleep.
Letting the passengers talk, with your own calm reply.
Lowering the bar on a hard day, and a plan for when it gets rough.
Your small lifts, for the flat days.
Your no-line.
Playing the tape forward when "just one" turns up.
Your break menu.
Your wind-down.
Making room for a heavy feeling.
And naming an old cue for what it is.
Now choose one.
The one you reach for most, or the one that surprised you by working.
Picture the last time you used it.
What happened to the craving?
That's the one to keep closest.
In a moment, your whole toolkit will be on your screen, in your own words.
Have a slow look.
You wrote all of it.
Then mark three weeks the way you marked the first two.
Something small, paid for with what you've kept.
Three weeks of practice.
It's yours now.
I'll see you in a few days.
